session_read: Second pass on the same day, and the tape did something worth naming: SMH +1.49% while the S&P and Nasdaq both closed red and VIX rose 6.4%. Semis led against a soft market rather than with it. But smith-signals put the day in its place -- COHR +9.75%, SNDK +8.97%, MRVL +6.2%, and not one of them crossed its own ATR-scaled threshold. A big day in aggregate; an ordinary one in each name's own volatility terms. Sentiment stepped down a full band inside ten hours, 81.8 extreme greed to 66.6 greed, so this morning's instruction to book profits into froth no longer applies. The structural news is not the tape. BX was fully exited after a seven-day round trip at essentially flat, and it was the only sizeable genuinely non-AI-capex holding in the book -- so diversification did not get repriced, it got deleted, and AI-capex mechanically rose to 89.66%. In its place came IONQ, which smith-thesis declines to call a diversifier at all: a different bet wearing the AI coat. Cash is 1.12% against a 5-15% band and deployable capital is zero, with NVDA reporting in eight sessions on the largest position in the book. Eleven of 35 names remain over their own ATR cap and aggregate open risk is 14.3% against a 10% ceiling. The desk's own proposal record now reads 14.3% on seven scored calls -- too small to be a verdict, too poor to ignore.
